title: UAE Says It Will Leave OPEC as Iran War Strains Oil Markets
partialText: The Gulf government has long complained about the group’s quotas, which officials believe unfairly limited its exports. Its departure is expected to weaken OPEC’s influence.

title: U.S. Gas Prices Hit Highest Level Since Beginning of War in Iran
partialText: The jump on Tuesday of 1.6 percent was the highest percentage increase in more than a month.

title: First Fully Loaded L.N.G. Tanker Since War Began Appears to Have Crossed the Strait
partialText: Liquefied natural gas transit has been effectively halted. A ship managed by Abu Dhabi’s state oil company managed to cross, said Kpler, a maritime data firm.

title: One Person Who Appears to Be Missing From King Charles’s U.S. Itinerary: Prince Harry
partialText: On a state visit designed in part to repair U.S.-British relations, King Charles’s schedule does not include plans to see his younger son, who lives in the United States with his family.

title: Epstein Scandal Looms Over King Charles’s U.S. Visit
partialText: The king is not planning to meet with victims of Jeffrey Epstein during his state visit because of “ongoing police inquiries” in Britain. The king’s brother was close to Mr. Epstein, a convicted sex offender.

title: What Elon Musk’s Clash With Sam Altman of OpenAI Is Really About
partialText: Mr. Musk’s lawsuit against Mr. Altman and OpenAI makes the case that all-encompassing greed is Silicon Valley’s defining feature.

title: Elon Musk Assails Sam Altman on Social Media Before OpenAI Trial
partialText: Mr. Musk’s posts on X have pushed his narrative that OpenAI has lost its way.

title: Here Are the Key Players in the OpenAI Trial
partialText: Elon Musk, Sam Altman and several other key artificial intelligence industry figures are slated to testify in the trial, which is expected to last several weeks.

title: Republicans Brace for Brutal Midterms as Trump’s Popularity Slips
partialText: The elections are still six months off, and some within the G.O.P. say there is still time to right the ship.

title: Graduates Reset Ambitions in Pursuit of First Jobs
partialText: Young people aiming to build careers are entering fields they had not considered to find their footing.

title: Military Quietly Accelerates Boat Strikes, Deploying More Aircraft
partialText: The military has increased the number of secret fixed-wing attack aircraft and armed MQ-9 Reaper drones, according to two people familiar with the matter.

title: Google Signs A.I. Deal With the Pentagon
partialText: The Pentagon has also signed deals for using A.I. on classified networks with OpenAI and Elon Musk’s xAI, amid a dispute with Anthropic.

title: Trump’s Top Child Care Official Wants a ‘Bonfire of Regulations’
partialText: As Americans face soaring child care costs, Alex Adams wants to loosen rules and tighten spending. Critics say that will harm children and shutter day cares.

title: Judge Says Maurene Comey Can Sue the Trump Administration for Firing Her
partialText: Ms. Comey, a former federal prosecutor who handled cases against Jeffery Epstein and Sean Combs, claimed in her suit that she was fired for political reasons.

title: Man Serving Life Without Parole for Georgia Robbery Is Freed, With Help From a Remorseful Prosecutor
partialText: Jessie Askew Jr. was sentenced to life without parole for a clumsy armed robbery with an unloaded gun. The man who sent him away was determined to bring him back home.

title: Adopting Trump’s Voice, Justice Dept. Asks Judge to Let Ballroom Proceed
partialText: The court filing links the security breach at the White House correspondents’ dinner to the lawsuit over President Trump’s ballroom project.

title: After Another Attempt on Trump’s Life, Is Political Violence on the Rise in the U.S.?
partialText: A conversation with Sean Westwood, a professor at Dartmouth who tracks political violence and Americans’ perceptions of it.

title: Ron Paul Saw The U.S. Mint’s Gold Problems Coming
partialText: And he’s basically fine with it.

title: U.S. Mint Buys Drug Cartel Gold and Sells It as ‘American’
partialText: As prices for the precious metal soar, the industry’s guardrails have broken down.

title: How We Traced U.S. Government Gold to a Drug Cartel
partialText: Three reporters followed supply chains to reveal that the U.S. Mint buys gold that comes from foreign pawn shops and drug dealers, then claims it is from the United States.

title: Stephen Colbert Gets Ready to Hang It Up
partialText: His late-night show ends next month after 11 seasons. He has lots of feelings.

title: Pregnancy With Lupus Is Risky. Would She Be Able to Carry Her Baby to Term?
partialText: Fatimah Shepherd’s kidneys were compromised, and pregnancy could send her into kidney failure.

title: Texas Lawmakers Question Camp Mystic’s Owners Over Deadly Flood
partialText: A state senator told the owners of the camp, where 28 people died, that they would no longer be allowed to operate the camp “if I can have anything to say with that.”

title: They Lost Their Homes in Cuba to the Communist Government. Will They Ever Get Them Back?
partialText: With Cuba in dire economic crisis, people whose properties were seized by its government decades ago say it’s time to resolve thorny compensation claims.

title: Why Do the Top Sushi Restaurants Leave Us So Bored, and So Broke?
partialText: What began in Japan as a quick, exciting working-class meal has morphed in American cities into an elaborate pampering of the well-heeled diner.

title: After an Assassination Attempt, a Grim Political Math Sets In
partialText: Assassination attempts against sitting presidents have tended to compound their political problems and isolate them from the public.

title: The Greatest Living Songwriters
partialText: We look at the list crafted by Times music writers.

title: Internet Restrictions Spur Russians to Openly Question Putin’s Moves
partialText: From beauty influencers to the token political opposition, Russians are openly questioning President Vladimir V. Putin’s moves to hamstring access.

title: UPS Won’t Bring Packages to Their Doors. Some Are Fed Up.
partialText: The United Parcel Service will not deliver inside two buildings on Staten Island where its drivers were assaulted decades ago. Residents are suing.

title: Man Pleads Guilty to Planning Attack at Taylor Swift Concert in Vienna
partialText: Austrian prosecutors said the man plotted in 2024 to set off a bomb outside the concert, which was later canceled. He and another man still face separate charges.

title: Lionel Rosenblatt Dies at 82; Led Daring Rescue of Vietnamese Refugees
partialText: In an unsanctioned mission, the Foreign Service officer helped evacuate about 200 South Vietnamese citizens from Saigon days before the city fell in 1975.
